sections.subtitle: Tangkhul Roman Alphabet & Vowel System
sections.content: Tangkhul utilizes a Latin-based phonetic alphabet introduced by Rev. William Pettigrew in 1897 and standardized by the Tangkhul Literature Society (TLS). Vowels: a, ā, e, i, o, u (short and long variants).
rules: Long vowels marked with macrons (ā, ē, ī, ō, ū) distinguish lexical minimal pairs (e.g., 'ram' [country] vs 'rām' [dry field]).
Diphthongs include: ei (meira), ai (kakhai), ao (vanao), ui (ngashui), oi (choi).

sections.subtitle: Consonant Inventory
sections.content: Stops: p, t, k, ph, th, kh, b, d, g. Nasals: m, n, ng. Fricatives: s, sh, h, z. Liquids: r, l. Glides: w, y.
rules: Velar nasal 'ng' can occur in syllable initial, medial, and coda positions (e.g., ngalei [earth], thingrong [tree]).
Initial consonant clusters predominantly involve liquids: pr-, tr-, kr-, phr-, thr-, khr-.

sections.subtitle: Gender Classification
sections.content: Tangkhul distinguishes biological and social gender through suffixed markers.
rules: Human Masculine: -mayar / -va (e.g., ngalava -> youth/man, naomayar -> boy/son).
Human Feminine: -shanao / -la (e.g., shanaonao -> girl/daughter, ava -> mother).
Animal Gender: Male suffix -khon / -mayara (simuk-mayara [bull]), Female suffix -lui / -shanao (simuk-lui [cow]).

sections.subtitle: Number & Pluralization
sections.content: Plurality is marked by appending collective and pluralizing postpositions.
rules: Plural suffix -bing / -bina: mi (person) -> mibing (people), vanao (bird) -> vanaobing (birds).
Collective marker -saikora (all/entirety): ngalanaobing saikora (all the young maidens).

sections.subtitle: Core Case Postpositions
sections.content: Tangkhul is an agglutinative postpositional language. Cases are attached directly to the noun phrase head.
rules: Nominative / Agentive: -na (e.g., I-na shansera -> I have read).
Accusative / Dative: -li (e.g., Ali milu -> Give to him; Vanaoli thei -> Saw the bird).
Instrumental: -eina (e.g., Ngaphei-eina tulu -> Cut with a machete).
Genitive / Possessive: -wui (e.g., Shim-wui kuiphung -> The pillar of the house).
Locative: -li (e.g., Kaphung-li pamda -> Residing on the mountain).
Ablative: -wui eina / -li eina (e.g., Ukhrul-wui eina kazat -> Coming from Ukhrul).
Comitative / Associative: -le / -nga (e.g., Amei-le kazat -> Walking together with brother).

sections.subtitle: Personal Pronouns
sections.content: First, second, and third person pronouns with singular, dual, and plural distinctions.
rules: 1st Person Singular: I (I, me) | Plural: Ithum (we, us) | Dual: Inikha (the two of us).
2nd Person Singular: Na (you) | Plural: Nathum (you all) | Dual: Nanikha (the two of you).
3rd Person Singular: Ana (he/she/it) | Plural: Amathum (they, them).
Demonstratives: Hi (this), Chi (that), Hili (here), Chili (there).

sections.subtitle: Adjective Formation & Comparison
sections.content: Most Tangkhul adjectives are derived from stative verbal roots prefixed with ka- or kha-.
rules: Positive: kapha (good), kakhangar (heavy), kathuk (deep), kahung (red).
Comparative suffix: -shang / -meila (kapha-meila -> better than).
Superlative suffix: -saikora wui meila / -tak (kaphatak -> the very best).

sections.subtitle: Cardinal Numerals
sections.content: 1: akha, 2: khani, 3: kathum, 4: mati, 5: phanga, 6: taruk, 7: shini, 8: shet, 9: chiko, 10: thara, 20: maku, 100: sha akha.
rules: Numerals follow the noun they qualify: mi kathum (three persons), thingrong mati (four trees).

sections.subtitle: Tense and Aspect Suffixes
sections.content: Tangkhul verbs carry inflectional suffixes indicating tense, aspect, and completion.
rules: Root verbs take prefix ka- / kha- in citation/infinitive form: kasa (to do), kazat (to go), kapam (to sit).
Present Simple / Habitual: -i / -ya (e.g., I zat-ya -> I go).
Present Continuous: -da lei (e.g., I pam-da lei -> I am sitting / waiting).
Past Perfective: -ser-re / -haowa (e.g., Ana zat-haowa -> He has departed).
Future Tense: -ra (e.g., Ithum shok-ra -> We will come out / emerge).
Imperative: -lu (positive: Salu -> Do it!), -kha (negative: Masalu -> Don't do it!).

sections.subtitle: Negative Particles
sections.content: Negation in Tangkhul is achieved primarily through the circumfix ma-...-mana.
rules: Declarative Negation: ma- [verb root] -mana (e.g., I ma-thei-mana -> I do not see/know).
Stative Negation: ma-kalei (is not / does not exist) vs lei (exists).
Prohibitive Imperative: ma- [verb root] -alu (e.g., Ma-zat-alu -> Do not go!).

sections.subtitle: Interrogative Particles
rules: Polar (Yes/No) questions: -la? (e.g., Na pamra-la? -> Will you stay?).
Wh-Questions: Khi (what), Kachida (where), Khipa (who), Khitharan (when), Khipakha (why).

sections.subtitle: Basic Constituent Order (SOV)
sections.content: Tangkhul strictly adheres to Subject-Object-Verb (SOV) typology with head-final syntactic trees.
rules: Standard word order: Subject + Object + Verb (e.g., Mayarnao-na [S] kharai [O] phungda lei [V] -> The man is carrying the basket).
Modifier precedes or follows based on category: Demonstratives precede, numerals and adjectives follow head nouns.
Honorific and polite particles: -sho, -rei, -meo signify mutual respect between kin and elders.

3_proverbs_and_idioms.tangkhul: Ra-chay-li theingui-shai-lu, rit-linga-lung khang-san-lu, kachi katha.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.literal: Roasting fruit when thirsty, or putting a stone on an already heavy load.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.english: Applies to a person who adds to his misery by repeated silly actions.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.hindi: प्यास लगने पर फल भूनना, या भारी बोझ पर पत्थर और लाद देना। (अपनी ही बेवकूफी से अपनी मुसीबत बढ़ाना / आफत मोल लेना।)
3_proverbs_and_idioms.parallel_english_proverb: Adding fuel to fire / Adding insult to injury

3_proverbs_and_idioms.tangkhul: Par-ki kaja-na shup-a, shup-ki kaja-na par-a, kachi katha.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.literal: Closing fist when one ought to open it, and opening when one ought to close.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.english: Applies to an ambitious, greedy person who thinks he can get a lot for nothing.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.hindi: जब हाथ खोलना चाहिए तब मुट्ठी भींचना, और जब बंद रखना चाहिए तब खोल देना। (लालच में सब कुछ गँवा बैठना / लालच बुरी बला है।)
3_proverbs_and_idioms.parallel_english_proverb: Covetousness over-reacheth itself

3_proverbs_and_idioms.tangkhul: Khamatha sa-gi ji-la fa nga-sa-thui-ho-wa, kachi katha.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.literal: Intending to do something good, but turning it into a complete mess.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.english: Applies to one who is unfortunate in any attempt to do something good.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.hindi: अच्छा करने चले थे पर काम और बिगड़ गया। (चौबे जी गए थे छब्बे बनने, दुबे बन कर आए।)
3_proverbs_and_idioms.parallel_english_proverb: The road to hell is paved with good intentions

3_proverbs_and_idioms.tangkhul: Nga-ley-a-kha shi-ley-tha, nga-yur-a-kha nga-wur tha, yay-a-kha nga-yay tha, kachi katha.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.literal: Unity is like wasps' nest on rock; discord is like moles' nest; shallowness is like a sieve.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.english: United we stand strong as a rock; divided we collapse like dry loam.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.hindi: एकता चट्टान पर बने ततैयों के छत्ते जैसी अटूट होती है; फूट पड़ने पर वह छछूंदर के बिल जैसी ढह जाती है।
3_proverbs_and_idioms.parallel_english_proverb: United we stand, divided we fall

3_proverbs_and_idioms.tangkhul: Tho-rachi-than thri, thai-ra chi-than tho, kachi katha.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.literal: Expecting feast and starving; expecting nothing and finding abundance.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.english: Receiving unexpected fortune when least expected, and disappointed when expectant.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.hindi: जब बहुत उम्मीद थी तब भूखे रहे, और जब कोई आस न थी तब छप्पर फाड़ कर मिला।
3_proverbs_and_idioms.parallel_english_proverb: Blessed are they that expect nothing, for they shall not be disappointed

3_proverbs_and_idioms.tangkhul: Mei kachot-li tara phungda kazat, kachi katha.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.literal: Carrying cold water while running towards a raging wild forest fire.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.english: Coming well-prepared with peace when tempers flare in clan gatherings.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.hindi: जंगल की आग बुझाने के लिए ठंडा पानी लेकर दौड़ना। (क्रोध में शांति का मरहम लगाना।)
3_proverbs_and_idioms.parallel_english_proverb: A soft answer turneth away wrath

3_proverbs_and_idioms.tangkhul: Lung-kui eina tonda kazat kha pheikhavai makalei, kachi katha.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.literal: Gliding down steep crags like river eel without arms or feet.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.english: Overcoming insurmountable natural obstacles through quiet perseverance and adaptability.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.hindi: बिना हाथ-पैर के भी ऊँची फिसलन भरी चट्टानों से सुरक्षित निकल जाना। (धैर्य और युक्ति से हर बाधा पार करना।)
3_proverbs_and_idioms.parallel_english_proverb: Where there is a will, there is a way

3_proverbs_and_idioms.tangkhul: Kaphung terrace-li yarshon-sakashung kha phei eina khon masamana.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.literal: Bowing low across terrace fields from dawn to dusk without complaining.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.english: Tireless diligence and quiet hard work bringing forth abundant harvest.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.hindi: सीढ़ीदार खेतों में भोर से शाम तक बिना उफ किए मेहनत करना। (परिश्रम ही सफलता की कुंजी है।)
3_proverbs_and_idioms.parallel_english_proverb: Hard work never kills a man / Diligence is the mother of good luck

3_proverbs_and_idioms.tangkhul: Khamang-tui ror-a-kha lungli chei-thada kapam, kachi katha.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.literal: A solemn promise once carved stands firmer than iron in mountain granite.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.english: A man of true honor never breaks his sworn word.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.hindi: मुँह से निकला वचन पत्थर की लकीर होता है। (प्राण जाए पर वचन न जाए।)
3_proverbs_and_idioms.parallel_english_proverb: An honest man's word is as good as his bond

3_proverbs_and_idioms.tangkhul: Ngashunli khangapa, ngaya tharan meira phungkazat, kachi katha.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.literal: Resting quietly by day, glowing brightly when darkness falls over the ridge.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.english: A humble and modest person whose true brilliance shines in times of crisis.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.hindi: दिन में शांत रहकर विपत्ति की रात में मशाल बनकर चमकना। (संकट में ही सच्चे वीर की पहचान होती है।)
3_proverbs_and_idioms.parallel_english_proverb: Adversity introduces a man to himself

3_proverbs_and_idioms.tangkhul: Maza khamahon tharan samkui eina phei mashun, kachi katha.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.literal: Striking the wooden mortar with rhythmic precision when golden paddy is ripe.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.english: Seizing the opportune moment when circumstances are ripe for harvest.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.hindi: धान पकते ही सही ताल में मूसल चलाना। (अवसर का लाभ उठाना / मौके पर चौका मारना।)
3_proverbs_and_idioms.parallel_english_proverb: Strike while the iron is hot

3_proverbs_and_idioms.tangkhul: Ava-wui ning eina tara kaphung thada ngakhum, kachi katha.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.literal: A mother's heart is a deep spring that never dries through summer drought.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.english: Unconditional motherly love and boundless familial devotion.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.hindi: माँ का स्नेह उस गहरे चश्मे जैसा है जो जेठ की दुपहरी में भी कभी नहीं सूखता।
3_proverbs_and_idioms.parallel_english_proverb: A mother's love is peace / Blood is thicker than water

3_proverbs_and_idioms.tangkhul: Minao-na kaphungli zat-la thing-kuisam ma-khat-mana, kachi katha.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.literal: Walking through high pine woods without disturbing dry fallen needles.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.english: Living so harmoniously and respectfully with nature that no harm is left behind.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.hindi: चीड़ के जंगल से इस तरह गुज़रना कि सूखी पत्ती भी न चटके। (प्रकृति के साथ पूर्ण सामंजस्य।)
3_proverbs_and_idioms.parallel_english_proverb: Leave nothing but footprints, take nothing but memories

3_proverbs_and_idioms.tangkhul: Sira kachangli khayang-eili phei khurli ngatak, kachi katha.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.literal: Gazing at the distant stars while stepping blind into the muddy ditch.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.english: Being so preoccupied with lofty daydreams that one forgets immediate duties.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.hindi: आसमान के तारे देखते-देखते पैरों के नीचे के गड्ढे में गिर जाना। (हवाई किले बनाना।)
3_proverbs_and_idioms.parallel_english_proverb: Keep your feet on the ground and your eyes on the stars

3_proverbs_and_idioms.tangkhul: Khamiyang-wui hamli tara kachui ma-tam-mana, kachi katha.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.literal: The guest pot in a hospitable home is never dry when a stranger knocks.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.english: Generous hospitality is the crown jewel of Tangkhul village character.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.hindi: अतिथि-सत्कार करने वाले के घर की हाँडी कभी खाली नहीं रहती। (अतिथि देवो भव।)
3_proverbs_and_idioms.parallel_english_proverb: Hospitality makes all men kin

3_proverbs_and_idioms.tangkhul: Khara-ngashat kakhon eina lami yām-thui-haowa, kachi katha.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.literal: The single sharp bark of the deer causes the lurking leopard to flee.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.english: Timely warning from the alert saves the entire community from disaster.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.hindi: काकड़ की एक तीखी पुकार से घात लगाए तेंदुए को भागना पड़ता है। (समय पर दी गई चेतावनी जान बचाती है।)
3_proverbs_and_idioms.parallel_english_proverb: Forewarned is forearmed

3_proverbs_and_idioms.tangkhul: Wung-wui akhonli ngaka kha mashunli zang-ra, kachi katha.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.literal: Heeding the quiet counsel of village elders keeps one upon the safe mountain trail.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.english: Respect for ancestral wisdom safeguards the youth from cliffside ruin.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.hindi: बुजुर्गों की बात मानकर चलने से पथरीले रास्तों पर कभी पैर नहीं फिसलते।
3_proverbs_and_idioms.parallel_english_proverb: Listen to the elders, for they have traveled the road

3_proverbs_and_idioms.tangkhul: Fa-kharar-na ngaya rurung-eili chimik kakhaya mathei, kachi katha.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.literal: The aged hound dozes by the fire, yet hears the softest tread in the yard.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.english: Old age brings sharpened inner perception and quiet intuition.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.hindi: बूढ़ा कुत्ता चूल्हे के पास सोता ज़रूर है, पर आँगन की मद्धिम आहट भी सुन लेता है।
3_proverbs_and_idioms.parallel_english_proverb: There is no fool like an old fool / Experience is the best teacher

3_proverbs_and_idioms.tangkhul: Khong-kharar kakhong tharan mayarnao saikora ngasot-ser-re, kachi katha.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.literal: When the great village log drum sounds, all men stand together as one wall.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.english: In times of collective defense, internal bickering vanishes instantly.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.hindi: जब गाँव का महा-नगाड़ा बजता है, तब सब मतभेद भूलकर एक दीवार बन जाते हैं।
3_proverbs_and_idioms.parallel_english_proverb: A common danger unites even foes

3_proverbs_and_idioms.tangkhul: Shongfa kharar-li kazat-a-kha aphei ma-chot-mana, kachi katha.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.literal: Walking along the ancient beaten footpath ensures sure feet that never stumble.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.english: Adhering to proven tradition brings security and peace of mind.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.hindi: पुरखों की बनी पगडंडी पर चलने से पाँव में कभी काँटा नहीं चुभता।
3_proverbs_and_idioms.parallel_english_proverb: Do not leave the old road for a new one

3_proverbs_and_idioms.tangkhul: Rap-kaphungli meikha kashur-thada ning kacham ngachon-ra, kachi katha.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.literal: Like smoked venison cured above the hearth, patience sweetens character.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.english: Trials endured with patience temper human character into pure gold.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.hindi: जैसे मचान पर धुएँ में सूखा माँस सालों चलता है, वैसे ही धैर्य से इंसान परिपक्व होता है।
3_proverbs_and_idioms.parallel_english_proverb: Patience is bitter, but its fruit is sweet

3_proverbs_and_idioms.tangkhul: Tangkhul-tui eina laa kasa-kha kaphung chiko ngakhum-ra, kachi katha.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.literal: Singing in ancestral Tangkhul tongue echoes across nine mountain ridges.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.english: Preserving one's native language preserves the very soul of the ancestors.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.hindi: मातृभाषा तंगखुल में गाया गया लोक-गीत नौ पहाड़ियों के पार तक गूँजता है।
3_proverbs_and_idioms.parallel_english_proverb: A language is the soul of its people

3_proverbs_and_idioms.tangkhul: Zimik kashung-tharan kachon phunglu, ngazing tharan chabi thumlu, kachi katha.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.literal: Work while the sun blazes high; lock the gate securely when dusk falls.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.english: Do all things in their proper season and balance labor with domestic rest.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.hindi: धूप रहते मेहनत करो, और शाम होते ही घर की अर्गला लगाओ। (समय पर काम और समय पर विश्राम।)
3_proverbs_and_idioms.parallel_english_proverb: Make hay while the sun shines

3_proverbs_and_idioms.tangkhul: Meikhu makalei-eili meira ma-ngaphar-mana, kachi katha.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.literal: Where there is no smoke rising, there can be no crackling campfire.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.english: Rumors rarely originate without some core grain of truth.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.hindi: जहाँ धुआँ नहीं, वहाँ आग नहीं हो सकती। (बिना आग के धुआँ नहीं उठता।)
3_proverbs_and_idioms.parallel_english_proverb: Where there's smoke, there's fire

3_proverbs_and_idioms.tangkhul: Kharai-kanao-li lungkui khangsan-a-kha kachir kakhai-ra, kachi katha.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.literal: Packing heavy river stones into a tiny cane basket breaks the bottom through.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.english: Imposing unbearable responsibilities upon the young or weak causes ruin.
3_proverbs_and_idioms.hindi: नन्ही टोकरी में भारी पत्थर लादने से उसकी तली फट जाती है। (क्षमता से अधिक बोझ न डालो।)
3_proverbs_and_idioms.parallel_english_proverb: The last straw breaks the camel's back

3_proverbs_and_idioms.hindi: छोटी बिल्ली के गुर्राने से जंगली सूअर कभी भयभीत नहीं होता। (खोखली धमकी से काम नहीं चलता।)

lunar_months.significance: Month of bitter mountain frost; elders gather around the hearth to plan terrace repairs and village festivals.
Clearing the hillside forest for jhum plots; burning dry brushwood before the first rains.
Sacred seed-sowing festival (Luira Phanit); invocations to the creator for bumper agricultural yields.
Terrace bund weeding; fresh spring showers; wild orchids burst into flower on high oak ridges.
Flooding the terraces with mountain streams; community transplanting of young paddy seedlings.
High monsoon downpours; rivers swell; village paths turn into cascading streams.
Midsummer weeding of terrace slopes; trapping river minnows and hill crabs in woven creels.
First green ears of hill corn ripen; roasted maize shared among children and elders by the fire.
Chumpha festival; opening the ancestral granary; blessing the first grains of autumn.
Golden terrace harvest month; reapers sing ancient folk ballads (Hao Laa) across the sunlit valley.
Threshing and winnowing golden paddy; wedding feasts and clan alliances celebrated.
Chilly winter winds blow; youth assemble in the Longshim dormitory for storytelling and riddling.

seasons.description: Wild apple blossoms, emerald slopes, return of songbirds, Luira seed blessing.
Continuous rains, mist-shrouded ridges, flooded rice terraces, thunder and lightning.
Golden rice fields, clear crisp blue skies, harvesting songs, Chumpha ceremonies.
Frosty mornings, woodsmoke in villages, warm hearth fires, Longshim oral banter.

5_conversational_phrases.context: Traditional mountain greeting called across paths.

5_conversational_phrases.english: Good morning! May peace be upon your morning.
How are you? Are you living in peace?
5_conversational_phrases.hindi: आप कैसे हैं? / क्या हाल-चाल है?

5_conversational_phrases.english: I am living in peace and good health.
5_conversational_phrases.hindi: मैं बिल्कुल ठीक और सकुशल हूँ।

5_conversational_phrases.english: Long time no see! We haven't met for seasons.
5_conversational_phrases.hindi: बहुत दिनों से भेंट नहीं हुई!

5_conversational_phrases.english: Which village do you come from?
5_conversational_phrases.hindi: आप किस गाँव / क्षेत्र से हैं?

5_conversational_phrases.english: I come from the misty hills of Ukhrul.
5_conversational_phrases.hindi: मैं उखरुल की पहाड़ियों से हूँ।

5_conversational_phrases.english: Do you speak the Tangkhul language?
5_conversational_phrases.hindi: क्या आप तंगखुल भाषा बोलते हैं?

5_conversational_phrases.english: Yes, I speak it fluently / No, I am learning.
5_conversational_phrases.tangkhul: Mha, I matuiya / Maningmanei, I tuitamda lei.
5_conversational_phrases.hindi: हाँ, मैं बोलता हूँ / नहीं, मैं अभी सीख रहा हूँ।

5_conversational_phrases.english: Please come inside to the hearth.
5_conversational_phrases.hindi: कृपया घर के भीतर अलाव के पास पधारें।
क्या आपने भोजन कर लिया है?

5_conversational_phrases.english: Thank you very deeply from my heart.
Farewell! Until we meet again on the trail.
5_conversational_phrases.hindi: अलविदा! फिर मिलेंगे / यात्रा शुभ हो!

5_conversational_phrases.english: May good dreams watch over your sleep tonight.
Where does this mountain path lead?
5_conversational_phrases.hindi: यह पहाड़ी पगडंडी कहाँ जाती है?

5_conversational_phrases.english: It climbs up directly to the summit of Shirui Kashong.
5_conversational_phrases.hindi: यह सीधे शिरुई काशोंग की चोटी पर जाती है।

songs.title_translation: Song of the Riverbank and Beloved Hills
songs.notes: Classic Tangkhul lyrical love song expressing yearning across mountain ranges, invoking the hills to lower their peaks that one may gaze upon beloved homeland.

songs.title: Yarra Laa: Yarshungwon
songs.title_translation: Youth Spring Awakening and Courting Chant
songs.collector: Dr. Ringkahao Horam / Tribal Research Institute

songs.title: Mangkhap Laa: Ngaphit Kazang
songs.notes: Traditional agricultural chant sung at the culmination of rice transplantation during Mangkhap Phanit, expressing thanksgiving for communal labor.

songs.title: Hao Pheichak Laa
songs.collector: H. Kamkhenthang / Directorate of Tribals Manipur
songs.notes: Antiphonal ceremonial warrior and celebration dance chant performed during major public gatherings and festival dances (Pheichak).

culture.title: Luira Phanit
culture.creator: Tangkhul Community Elders
culture.notes: Prime annual agricultural spring festival celebrated in January/February marking the inauguration of the agricultural cycle. Features ceremonial sod-turning by the Awunga, wrestling (Kaphung), folk dances, and sacred prayers.

culture.title: Chumpha Phanit
culture.creator: Tangkhul Women & Community
culture.notes: Post-harvest thanksgiving festival celebrated in December. Specially honors women as custodians of the grain; involves ceremonial transfer of granary responsibility and blessings for food security.

culture.title: Mangkhap Phanit
culture.creator: Tangkhul Agriculturalists
culture.notes: Mid-summer festival celebrated in July following completion of arduous paddy transplantation. Serves as community celebration and period of rest before weeding.

culture.title: Thisham Phanit
culture.creator: Tangkhul Ancestral Lineages
culture.notes: Traditional memorial feast held in winter honoring family members who passed away during the preceding year. Pine torches are lit along pathways to guide departed spirits to Kasa Akhava (ancestral realm).

culture.title: Yarra Phanit
culture.creator: Longshim Youths
culture.notes: Spring youth celebration celebrated within village dormitories (Longshim) featuring feasting, folk song exchanges, and socialization among youth.

culture.title: Proverb on Elder Counsel: Hanna hannui shaiphamei
culture.title_translation: Tender Greens are Tasty, but Elder Wisdom is Sweeter
culture.creator: Traditional Oral Lore (Kasomwoshi 1991, Kanrei 1978)
culture.notes: Original saying: 'Hanna hannui shaiphamei, tuiva arartui phamei.' Teaches that while youth possesses vigor and novelty, seasoned elder counsel holds enduring guidance for navigating life.

culture.title: Proverb on Restorative Justice: Nguihaowada
culture.title_translation: A Person Cannot be Drowned for a Mistake
culture.creator: Traditional Legal Lore (Kasomwoshi 1991)
culture.notes: Original saying: 'Nguihaowada masi kongra li machikhai paimana.' Emphasizes that traditional Tangkhul customary jurisprudence values restitution, reform, and reconciliation over cruel or irreversible punishment.

culture.title: Proverb on the Power of Words: Khamor kachangna
culture.title_translation: Sharp Words Pierce Deeper than Spear Wounds
culture.creator: Traditional Oral Wisdom (Pettigrew 1918, Sira 1991)
culture.notes: Original saying: 'Khamor kachangna phei ngazekli.' Warns that harsh words inflict psychological injuries that endure far longer than physical wounds.

culture.title: Proverb on Disproportionate Fuss: Faphei meikachui
culture.title_translation: Making a Fuss Like a Dog with a Singed Paw
culture.creator: Traditional Oral Idiom (Kasomwoshi 1991)
culture.notes: Original saying: 'Faphei meikachui thalakli.' Metaphorical proverb ridiculing someone who creates theatrical drama over a trivial inconvenience.

culture.title: Proverb on Patriotism: Ava ram shungli
culture.title_translation: No Love is Greater Than Love for the Motherland
culture.creator: Traditional Patriotic Maxim (Tangkhul Literature Society)
culture.notes: Original saying: 'Ava ram shungli leishat mathamei.' A bedrock traditional saying expressing reverence and loyalty to ancestral lands.

culture.title: Proverb on Resilience: Shiyan mahara
culture.creator: Traditional Blacksmith & Moral Lore
culture.notes: Original saying: 'Shiyan mahara ngalemli.' Drawing on indigenous metallurgical crafts, it teaches that hardships fortify moral character.

culture.title: Longshim Youth Dormitory System
culture.creator: Tangkhul Ancestral Village Community
culture.notes: Central indigenous institution divided into Mayarshim (boys dormitory) and Ngashim (girls dormitory). Functioned as educational center for transmitting oral songs, customary discipline, weaving, and woodcraft.

culture.title: Hangva Council of Elders
culture.creator: Tangkhul Clan Representatives
culture.notes: Customary governing council of village clan leaders (Hangva) assisting the Awunga (hereditary chief). Mediates property boundaries, inter-clan disputes, and customary fines.

culture.title: Yarnao Agricultural Labour Exchange
culture.creator: Tangkhul Youth & Farming Peer Groups
culture.notes: Mutual assistance cooperative where groups of young men and women rotate work across each member's terraced fields during sowing and harvesting seasons.

culture.title: Manom Marriage Custom and Dowry
culture.creator: Tangkhul Clan Exogamy Custodians
culture.notes: Exogamous clan marriage system requiring formal negotiation between families, presentation of handwoven shawls (Manom), brass gong gifts, and communal feast.

culture.title: Haora Men's Traditional Shawl
culture.creator: Tangkhul Master Weavers
culture.notes: Renowned handwoven cotton shawl with white, red, and black bands, featuring delicate hand-stitched Ramik (eye of peacock) patterns along the edges. Worn by men during festivals.

culture.title: Chonkhom Women's Traditional Shawl
culture.creator: Tangkhul Weaving Guilds
culture.notes: Prestigious handloom shawl featuring red base with dark horizontal stripes. Highly valued as bridal attire and ceremonial wear.

culture.title: Seichan Kashan Wraparound Skirt
culture.creator: Tangkhul Women Weavers
culture.notes: Intricately patterned wraparound skirt (Kashan) featuring ancestral motifs, traditionally worn by women during cultural gatherings and dance performances.

culture.title: Longkhor Conical Basket Craft
culture.creator: Tangkhul Bamboo Craftsmen
culture.notes: Artisanal hand-woven conical bamboo basket used with head tumpline for transporting paddy, firewood, and harvest produce across mountainous terrain.

culture.title: Khamasit Sacred Taboo Observance
culture.creator: Traditional Religious Guardians
culture.notes: Solemn days of village boundary closure and ritual stillness where agricultural tasks and travel cease to appease natural spirits. Specific esoteric incantations remain restricted.

culture.title: Luira Shimlut-Kaphung Sod-Turning Rite
culture.creator: Awunga (Village Chief) of Hunphun
culture.notes: Ceremonial act performed at dawn on the first day of Luira Phanit where the village chief turns the first clod of soil and sows the first seeds before any villager may plant.

culture.title: Shimreishang Kala Maitonphi Tradition
culture.title_translation: The Legendary Phungcham Love Ballad Tradition
culture.creator: Phungcham Village Oral Historians
culture.notes: The 17th-century Phungcham tragic romance tradition. Preserves archaic dialect vocabulary, wedding customs, mourning rituals, and poetic verses between Shimreishang and Maitonphi.

culture.title: Makhel Dispersal Migration Narrative
culture.title_translation: Oral Tradition of Common Origin at Makhel
culture.creator: Tangkhul Village Raconteurs
culture.notes: Ancestral tradition recounting the migration of the Tangkhul clans from Makhel, the sacred dispersal under the wild pear tree, and traditional covenants of unity.

culture.title: Champhung Village Sacred Monolith Rites
culture.creator: Champhung Community Elders
culture.notes: Fieldwork documentation on commemorative stone pulling and monolith erection rites in Champhung village. Candidate record awaiting full elder review and clan clearance.

culture.title: Dharreo Phanit
culture.creator: Tangkhul Farming Elders
culture.notes: Autumn pre-harvest festival celebrated in October before sickle touches the golden grain. Ritual invocations petition the Creator for protection against devastating wind, hail, and vermin before harvest.

culture.title: Khamang Phanit
culture.title_translation: Communal River Fishing & Walnut Bark Festival
culture.creator: Hundung & Ukhrul River Troupes
culture.notes: Autumn communal river expedition where river channels are treated with pulverized wild walnut root (Ngasung) to stun fish, accompanied by forest fellowship banquets.

culture.title: Maran Kasa Feast of Merit & Tarang Monument
culture.title_translation: The Feast of Merit Cycle and Sacred Post Erection
culture.creator: Tangkhul Hereditary Nobility & Benefactors
culture.notes: The pinnacle institutional feast cycle hosted by a generous benefactor for the entire village, granting the lifelong cultural privilege of erecting the sacred forked Tarang post and adorning one's home as a Lengcheng Shim.

culture.title: Longpi Hamlei Black Stone Pottery
culture.creator: Longpi (Loree) Master Potters
culture.notes: Renowned ancient pottery crafted without a potter's wheel using ground black serpentinite rock (leshong lung) and weathered clay (sali), fired outdoors and polished with Chiron/Mahasa leaves.

culture.title: Lengcheng Shim Traditional Architecture & Roof-Horns
culture.title_translation: Traditional High-Status House Architecture with Crossed Roof-Horns
culture.creator: Tangkhul Master Woodcarvers & Awunga Builders
culture.notes: Elite Tangkhul house architecture featuring crossed carved wooden horns (Lengcheng Kui) extending from the roof ridge, with facade planks intricately carved with mithun heads and solar symbols.

culture.title: Kalhang & Marem Brine Well Salt-Making
culture.title_translation: Indigenous Brine Well Salt Extraction & Cake Manufacturing
culture.creator: Kalhang & Marem Salt Guilds
culture.notes: Historical mineral salt manufacture from natural deep mountain brine wells (Machi kong), evaporated in circular iron cauldrons to form flat salt cakes historically used as currency.

culture.title: Proverb on Inner Wisdom: Theikahaina kaphaningli
culture.title_translation: The Wise Perceive with the Mind, the Foolish with the Eyes
culture.creator: Traditional Oral Philosophy (Kasomwoshi 1991, Pettigrew 1918)
culture.notes: Original saying: 'Theikahaina kaphaningli, matheikahaina mikli.' Teaches that wise judgment looks beneath outward appearance to perceive true moral character.

culture.title: Proverb on Human Nature: Khare khangatei makhangaza
culture.title_translation: Habit is Hard to Alter, Generational Transformation Requires Wisdom
culture.creator: Traditional Moral Philosophy (Kasomwoshi 1991)
culture.notes: Original saying: 'Khare khangatei makhangaza, thot khangatei maharmana.' Teaches patience in governance and personal transformation, noting that character reform takes enduring perseverance.

culture.title: Tangkhul Traditional Prayers & Invocations (Hai-kapha kala Seikha-kapha)
culture.title_translation: Comprehensive Compendium of Tangkhul Invocations, Blessing Prayers, and Sacred Chants
culture.creator: Tangkhul Community Elders & Traditional Invocators
culture.notes: Comprehensive documentation of traditional Tangkhul invocations (Hai-kapha) and blessing chants (Seikha-kapha) addressed to the Supreme Creator (Varivara), mountain spirits, hearth dedication, agricultural blessings, and ancestral spirits.

culture.title: Tangkhul Sacred Rituals, Ceremonies & Taboos (Phanit, Kakhangaso kala Khamasit)
culture.title_translation: Master Archive of Tangkhul Lifecycle Ceremonies, Agrarian Rites, and Sacred Taboo Observances
culture.creator: Tangkhul Hereditary Custodians & Village Elders
culture.notes: Comprehensive archival codification of Tangkhul ceremonial life: agrarian seasonal rites (Luira, Chumpha, Mangkhap, Dharreo), human lifecycle rituals (birth, naming, youth dormitory induction, marriage, house dedication, death), prestige feast cycles (Maran Kasa), chiefly enthronement, and sacred taboo (Khamasit / Genna) observances.

culture.title: Tangkhul Clan System, Kinship & Social Order (Shang, Shangnao kala Hangva)
culture.title_translation: Comprehensive Monograph on Tangkhul Patrilineal Clans, Exogamy Rules, Hereditary Governance, and Longshim Institutions
culture.creator: Tangkhul Clan Genealogists, Hangva Council & Cultural Scholars
culture.publisher: Documented in Horam 1977, Hodson 1911, Ruivah 1993, Shimray 2000
culture.village: All Tangkhul Regions (Northern Raphei, Southern Kamo, Western Remva, Eastern Somra)
culture.notes: Foundational sociological and anthropological study of Tangkhul Naga social structure. Clarifies the complete absence of a caste system, examining instead the democratic patrilineal clan (Shang / Shangnao) structure, strict clan exogamy, village governance (Awunga and Hangva council), and youth dormitory institutions (Longshim).

history.title: Pettigrew's Arrival and Establishment of First Mission School
history.title_translation: Founding of First Formal School in Hunphun / Ukhrul
history.creator: Rev. William Pettigrew & Hunphun Community
history.notes: Rev. William Pettigrew arrived in Ukhrul after being barred from the Imphal valley by the Political Agent. With permission from Hunphun Chief Raihao, he opened the first vernacular school, introducing Roman script literacy to the Tangkhuls.

history.title: 66th Manipur Labour Corps Deployment in World War I
history.title_translation: Tangkhul Service in France During the Great War
history.creator: Tangkhul Labour Corps Veterans & R.S. Ruichumhao
history.notes: Over a thousand hillmen from Manipur, including hundreds of Tangkhuls led by R.S. Ruichumhao, volunteered for service in France, gaining broad international exposure and accelerating post-war community consciousness.

history.title: Battle of Sangshak in World War II
history.title_translation: The Sangshak Delaying Action
history.creator: Allied Forces, 50th Parachute Brigade & Sangshak Villagers
history.notes: Fierce six-day delaying battle fought across the Sangshak plateau by the 50th Indian Parachute Brigade against the Japanese 31st Division, critically blunting the enemy drive towards Kohima and Imphal.

history.title: Establishment of the Tangkhul Literature Society (TLS)
history.title_translation: Formation of Tangkhul Language Standardization Body
history.creator: Tangkhul Elders & Educators
history.notes: Pioneering assembly of teachers, pastors, and elders that established the Tangkhul Literature Society to standardize orthography, publish vernacular readers, and curate the literary heritage.

history.title: Publication of the First Tangkhul Primer
history.title_translation: Inauguration of Tangkhul Print Literature
history.creator: Rev. William Pettigrew
history.notes: First printed reading textbook adapting the Roman alphabet to Tangkhul phonology, inaugurating formal vernacular education across the Manipur eastern hills.

history.title: Rev. William Pettigrew (1869–1943)
history.title_translation: Pioneering Missionary, Linguist, and Educator
history.creator: Biographical Documentation (Pettigrew 1918, Horam 1977)
history.notes: British educational missionary and linguist who lived in Ukhrul from 1896 to 1933. Reduced the Tangkhul Ukhrul dialect to Roman script, translated foundational texts, and authored the 1918 Grammar and Dictionary.

history.title: Major Relengnao Bob Khating (1912–1990)
history.title_translation: Soldier, Administrator, and Diplomat
history.creator: Biographical Archives of Manipur & Northeast India
history.notes: Distinguished Tangkhul military officer (MC, MBE) and Indian diplomat. Led the historic 1951 expedition establishing Indian civil administration in Tawang (Arunachal Pradesh) and later served as Indian Ambassador to Burma.

history.title: R.S. Ruichumhao (c. 1880–1935)
history.title_translation: Early Tangkhul Scholar, Educator, and WWI Corps Leader
history.creator: Community Oral History & Mission Archives
history.notes: One of the earliest educated Tangkhuls who assisted William Pettigrew in translation work, served as a prominent leader of the Labour Corps in France during WWI, and pioneered early community welfare initiatives.

history.title: Awunga Raihao of Hunphun
history.title_translation: Chief of Hunphun Who Granted Mission School Sanction
history.creator: Hunphun Village Oral & Archival History
history.notes: Hereditary Chief (Awunga) of Hunphun whose visionary statesmanship permitted Rev. Pettigrew to reside in Hunphun in 1896, guaranteeing village protection and enrolling initial students in the first formal school.

history.title: Ukhrul / Hunphun Settlement
history.title_translation: Traditional and Administrative Center of the Tangkhuls
history.creator: Settlement Gazetteer Documentation
history.publisher: Gazetteer of Manipur & British Colonial Administration
history.notes: Spiritual, educational, and political center of the Tangkhul region. Formed historically by the Hunphun clan lineages and established as the colonial hill sub-divisional headquarters in the early 20th century.

history.title: Makhel Dispersal Site
history.title_translation: Sacred Ancestral Dispersal Point
history.creator: Pan-Naga Ancestral Tradition
history.notes: Sacred historical settlement recognized across Tangkhul, Mao, Maram, and related Naga communities as the common parting point of lineages, marked by the sacred wild pear tree (Chutebu) and megalithic stone covenants.

history.title: Sangshak Ridge Settlement
history.title_translation: Historic Fortress Village and Battlefield
history.creator: Settlement & Military History Documentation
history.notes: Strategic mountain settlement in western Ukhrul district with deep historical traditions of village defense, which became world-famous during the crucial March 1944 delaying action against Japanese forces.

history.title: Shirui Kashong Sacred Mountain
history.title_translation: The Sacred Sentinel Peak of the Tangkhuls
history.creator: Tangkhul Geographical & Ecological Lore
history.notes: Prominent 2,835-meter ancestral peak overlooking Ukhrul. Revered in traditional songs and folklore as a sacred mountain guardian; endemic home of the rare Shirui Lily (Lilium mackliniae).

history.title: Phungcham Ancestral Village
history.title_translation: Ancient Cradle Settlement of Northern Tangkhuls
history.creator: Phungcham Oral Historians
history.notes: One of the oldest continuously settled northern villages. Custodian of distinctive dialectal phonology and the setting of the legendary 17th-century love ballad Shimreishang Kala Maitonphi.

history.title: Champhung Historic Village
history.title_translation: Western Tangkhul Megalithic Settlement
history.creator: Champhung Community Custodians
history.notes: Historically significant western village possessing intact traditions of commemorative stone-pulling and megalith erection, with an archaic dialect distinct from standard Ukhrul speech.

history.title: Hundung (Hungdung) Village
history.title_translation: Ancestral Southern Gateway Settlement
history.creator: Hundung Oral Historians & Royal Chronicles
history.notes: Strategic southern gateway to Ukhrul. Foremost in oral traditions commemorating the fraternal bond between the Tangkhul hill ancestors and the Meitei rulers of the valley.

history.title: Tangkhul Clan Migration Traditions from Makhel
history.title_translation: Ancestral Dispersal and Settlement Across Ukhrul Hills
history.creator: Tangkhul Clan Raconteurs
history.notes: Foundational oral narrative describing the migration from Makhel, the parting rituals, and the establishment of ancestral settlements across Hundung, Hunphun, Phungcham, and the eastern frontier ridges.

history.title: Major McCulloch's 1859 Tangkhul Wordlist Documentation
history.title_translation: Earliest Recorded Tangkhul Comparative Wordlist
history.creator: Major M. McCulloch
history.notes: Earliest known published linguistic record of Tangkhul vocabulary, documenting 150+ comparative lexical entries compiled by the Political Agent in Manipur.

history.title: Grierson's Linguistic Survey of India Tangkhul Classification
history.title_translation: First Systematic Comparative Linguistic Survey of Tangkhul
history.creator: Sir George A. Grierson
history.notes: Comprehensive survey classifying Tangkhul within the Tibeto-Burman language family (Kuki-Chin-Naga group), containing grammatical sketches, vocabulary lists, and comparative dialect texts.

history.title: Publication of Pettigrew's Grammar and Dictionary (1918)
history.title_translation: Seminal Tangkhul-English Lexicographical Milestone
history.creator: Rev. William Pettigrew
history.notes: Monumental 400-page work providing the first comprehensive grammar and bilingual dictionary of Tangkhul (Ukhrul dialect), establishing standard spelling conventions and pedagogical standards.

history.title: Cheitharol Kumbaba (Royal Chronicle of Manipur) Tangkhul Records
history.title_translation: Historical Chronicle Entries on Tangkhul-Meitei Relations
history.creator: Royal Scribes of the Palace of Kangla
history.publisher: Kangla Palace Archives / Manipur State Archives
history.notes: Centuries-long official court chronicle recording diplomatic ties, coronation ceremonial exchanges of Haora cloths, trade routes, and customary treaties between valley kings and Tangkhul chiefs.

history.title: Formation of the Tangkhul Long (Tangkhul Naga Long)
history.title_translation: Unification of Tangkhul Village Councils into Apex Body
history.creator: Tangkhul Village Chiefs and Elders
history.notes: Customary and democratic union of traditional village councils (Hangva) into a unified apex governance body (Tangkhul Long) representing the collective social, customary, and cultural interests of the tribe.

history.title: Oral Tradition of the Elder Brother and Younger Brother
history.title_translation: Narrative of Fraternal Kinship Between Hills and Valley
history.creator: Tangkhul & Meitei Oral Tradition Custodians
history.notes: Widespread traditional narrative recounting common ancestry where the elder brother remained in the mountainous hills (Tangkhul) while the younger brother migrated to settle the valley (Meitei).

history.title: Commemorative Monolith Inscription at Khangkhui Cave
history.title_translation: Fieldwork Candidate Record on Khangkhui Archaeological Site
history.creator: Field Archaeological Team & Khangkhui Elders
history.notes: Candidate archaeological record concerning Upper Paleolithic stone tools and ancestral commemorative markers documented near Khangkhui Mangsor cave; awaiting corroboration and archaeological clearance.

history.title: The Ngayira Spring Baptism and Foundation of Phungyo Baptist Church
history.title_translation: Inauguration of Christianity and First Church in Manipur Hills
history.creator: Rev. William Pettigrew & 12 Pioneer Converts
history.publisher: Documented in Pettigrew 1918, Horam 1977, Phungyo Church Centenary 2001
history.notes: On September 29, 1901, Rev. William Pettigrew baptized the first 12 Tangkhul converts at the Ngayira spring pond in Ukhrul, formally founding Phungyo Baptist Church, the first Christian church in the state of Manipur.

history.title: 1891 Anglo-Manipur War and Tangkhul Pass Neutrality Pacts
history.title_translation: Defense of Hill Passes During the Anglo-Manipur Conflict
history.creator: Hunphun and Hundung Village Councils
history.publisher: Documented in Grimwood 1891, Hodson 1911, Manipur State Archives
history.notes: During the Anglo-Manipur War of 1891 following the palace uprising in Imphal, Tangkhul village councils maintained strategic defensive neutrality, safeguarding mountain passes and protecting non-combatants retreating across the eastern hills.

history.title: Yangmaso Shaiza (1923–1984)
history.title_translation: First Tribal Chief Minister of Manipur and Statesman
history.creator: Biographical Archives of Manipur Legislative Assembly
history.publisher: Government of Manipur & Manipur Hills Union Archives
history.notes: Distinguished statesman from Ukhrul (grandson of Hunphun Chief Raihao) who founded the Manipur Hills Union and served as the fifth Chief Minister of Manipur (1974, 1977–1979), the first leader from the hill tribes to hold the office, championing ethnic harmony and hill autonomy.

history.title: Nungbi (Luireishimphung) Black Stone Pottery Settlement
history.title_translation: Ancestral Craft Cradle of Wheel-less Serpentinite Pottery
history.creator: Nungbi Pottery Custodians & Archaeological Survey
history.publisher: Documented in Horam 1977, Roy 1961, Manipur Cultural Directorate
history.notes: Historic northern settlement celebrated globally for its ancient craft of hand-shaped black stone pottery (Hampai), fashioned without a potter's wheel from a sacred blend of weathered serpentinite stone and weathered clay.

history.title: Chingjaroi (Swemi) Tri-Hamlet Ancestral Settlement
history.title_translation: Northern Frontier Citadel of Megaliths and Customary Defense
history.creator: Chingjaroi Village Oral Historians
history.notes: Formidable northern border settlement comprising three historic hamlets (Khullen, CV, Raphiei). Renowned for ancient stone megaliths (Lungchei), stone-dragging roads, and heroic defense pacts along the ancestral Naga frontier.

history.title: Huishu Ancient Iron-Smelting & Border Settlement
history.title_translation: Myanmar Frontier Hearth of Metallurgy and Atonal Speech
history.creator: Huishu Clan Elders & Linguistic Fieldwork Surveys
history.notes: Historic frontier settlement near the international border with Myanmar. Renowned as an ancient center of traditional bloomery iron smelting, brine salt springs, and the archaic atonal Huishu dialect preserving Proto-Tangkhulic consonants.

history.title: The Longshim (Traditional Youth Dormitory Institution)
history.title_translation: Ancestral Academy of Civic Lore, Music, and Martial Arts
history.creator: Tangkhul Cultural Historians & Elders
history.notes: Paramount ancestral socio-educational institution of every Tangkhul village. Functioned as the community dormitory and academy where youth mastered village defense, customary jurisprudence, epic ballads (Khararchan), weaving, and agricultural rituals.

history.title: Capt. Pemberton's 1835 Report on the Eastern Frontier
history.title_translation: Earliest Official British Survey of the Tangkhul Country
history.creator: Captain R. Boileau Pemberton
history.notes: Landmark 1835 British military and geographical survey published in Calcutta providing the first official cartographic and ethnographic description of the Tangkhul (Luhuppa) hills, village fortifications, pass routes, and trade to Burma.

dictionaries.title: Tangkhul Naga Grammar and Dictionary (Ukhrul Dialect) with Illustrative Sentences

sections.chapter: Chapter 1: Kazing kala Ngalei Kasa (Creation of Heaven and Earth)

verses.tangkhul: Hau-kaphokli Varivarana kazing kala ngalei kasa.
verses.english: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.
verses.hindi: आदि में परमेश्वर ने आकाश और पृथ्वी की सृष्टि की।

verses.tangkhul: Kala ngaleiya mai-kaphā makaleida ngazishingli leisai; kala Varivarawui Mangkhapna tarawui mai-ngathangli rurungsai.
verses.english: And the earth was without form, and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.
verses.hindi: और पृथ्वी बेडौल और सुनसान पड़ी थी, और गहरे जल के ऊपर अंधियारा था; और परमेश्वर की आत्मा जल के ऊपर मण्डलाती थी।

verses.tangkhul: Kala Varivarana hosa: 'Meira ngaphar-lu!' kala meira ngapharsai.
verses.english: And God said, Let there be light: and there was light.
verses.hindi: तब परमेश्वर ने कहा, 'उजियाला हो', तो उजियाला हो गया।

verses.tangkhul: Kala Varivarana meira chi kapha theisai; kala Varivarana meira eina ngazishingli kharar-hai-sai.
verses.english: And God saw the light, that it was good: and God divided the light from the darkness.
verses.hindi: और परमेश्वर ने उजियाले को देखा कि अच्छा है; और परमेश्वर ने उजियाले को अंधियारे से अलग किया।

sections.chapter: Psalm 23: Isha-wui Mayonpa (The Lord is my Shepherd)

verses.tangkhul: Isha-wui Varivara Iwui Mayonpasai; I khikha machot-mana.
verses.english: The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want.
verses.hindi: यहोवा मेरा चरवाहा है; मुझे कुछ घटी न होगी।

verses.tangkhul: Ana ili pui-kaphā ngaleili pam-ngasakya; Ana ili tara-khamashungli mayon-zatta.
verses.english: He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters.
verses.hindi: वह मुझे हरी-हरी चराइयों में बैठाता है; वह मुझे सुखदाई जल के झरने के पास ले चलता है।

verses.tangkhul: Ana iwui ningli kathara mi; Awui mingwui vang mashunkasawui shongfali ili pashun-ngasakya.
verses.english: He restoreth my soul: he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name's sake.
verses.hindi: वह मेरे जी में जी ले आता है; और अपने नाम के निमित्त मुझे धर्म के मार्गों में ले चलता है।

verses.tangkhul: I kathi-wui ngazishing kongkhurli zat-la khikha ma-ngachee-mana, maramchilu Na ilei; Nawui thei-changna ili ningphā-mi.
verses.english: Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.
verses.hindi: चाहे मैं मृत्यु की छाया से होकर चलूँ, तो भी हानि से न डरूँगा, क्योंकि तू मेरे साथ रहता है; तेरी सोंटी और तेरी लाठी से मुझे शांति मिलती है।

verses.tangkhul: Na nawui ning saikora eina Varivarali ning-nganilu; nawui phaning-shonli ma-nganip-alu.
verses.english: Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.
verses.hindi: तू अपनी सम्पूर्ण समझ पर भरोसा न रखना, वरन सम्पूर्ण मन से यहोवा पर भरोसा रखना।

verses.tangkhul: Nawui shongfa saikorali Ali theikhuilu, kala Ana nawui shongfali mashun-ngasak-ra.
verses.english: In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.
verses.hindi: उसी को अपने सब मार्गों में स्मरण रखना, तब वह तेरे लिये सीधा मार्ग निकालेगा।

sections.book: John Kahona Kasa (Gospel of John / यूहन्ना रचित सुसमाचार)
sections.chapter: Chapter 1 & 3: Tui Kathara (The Eternal Word & Grace)

verses.tangkhul: Kaphung-kachungwui thotli Tui li-li-sai, kala Tuichi Varivarali lei, kala Tuichi Varivarasai.
verses.english: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
verses.hindi: आदि में वचन था, और वचन परमेश्वर के साथ था, और वचन परमेश्वर था।

verses.tangkhul: Kala Tuichi miwung thot sakahaida i-wui ngachaili pamsai, Ava-wui Mayar Makazawui mathi kachicham thotna.
verses.english: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, full of grace and truth.
verses.hindi: और वचन देहधारी हुआ; और अनुग्रह और सच्चाई से परिपूर्ण होकर हमारे बीच में डेरा किया।

verses.tangkhul: Varivarana okathui-hi leishilak-da, Awui Naomayar Makaza akhana mili, khipakha Ali ning-nganira chichi makashiman-eili haring kapha thot phangra.
verses.english: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.
verses.hindi: क्योंकि परमेश्वर ने जगत से ऐसा प्रेम रखा कि उसने अपना एकलौता पुत्र दे दिया, ताकि जो कोई उस पर विश्वास करे, वह नाश न हो, परन्तु अनन्त जीवन पाए।

kandas.title: Bala Kanda: Ramwui Naokaphok kala Janakwui Kazei (Childhood & The Great Bow)
kandas.hindi_title: बाल काण्ड: राम जन्म, ताड़का वध एवं धनुष भंग
kandas.summary: King Dasharatha of Ayodhya performs the sacred rite; Rama is born endowed with divine virtue. Sage Vishvamitra brings Rama and Lakshmana to defend the hermitage from demons. At Mithila, Rama bends and breaks the mighty Bow of Shiva and weds Janaka's daughter Sita.

stanzas.tangkhul: Ayodhya ramli Dasharatha awunga mashunta pamda leisai; Awui naomayar khare Ramna kaphā saikora phungda ngashunsai.
stanzas.english: In sacred Ayodhya ruled virtuous King Dasharatha; his firstborn son Rama was gifted with every heavenly virtue.
stanzas.hindi: पवित्र अयोध्या नगरी में धर्मात्मा राजा दशरथ राज्य करते थे; उनके ज्येष्ठ पुत्र राम दिव्य सद्गुणों से सुशोभित थे।

stanzas.tangkhul: Mithila ramli Janak awungana Shiva-wui kazei-kharei phungsai; Ramna kazei chi phuklaga khup-kakhai eina Sita-le phankahai thot sasai.
stanzas.english: In Mithila, King Janaka brought forth the mighty Bow of Shiva; Rama lifted and broke it, wedding beautiful Sita in joyous celebration.
stanzas.hindi: मिथिला में राजा जनक ने शिव का भारी धनुष प्रस्तुत किया; राम ने उसे सहज ही उठाकर भंग कर दिया और सीता से विवाह रचाया।

kandas.title: Ayodhya Kanda: Kaphungli Kazat (The Banishment & Forest Exile)
kandas.hindi_title: अयोध्या काण्ड: वन गमन एवं धर्म निष्ठा
kandas.summary: Queen Kaikeyi claims her two boons, demanding Bharata's coronation and Rama's fourteen-year exile. Rama receives the command without sorrow or malice, honoring his father's truth. Sita and faithful brother Lakshmana accompany him into the deep woods.

stanzas.tangkhul: Ramna ning-kakachai makaleida ava-wui tui nganisai; 'Ava-wui mashunkasa phungkhavai I kaphungli thara-mati kum pamra.'
stanzas.english: Without bitterness, Rama obeyed his father's vow: 'To uphold my father's truth, I will dwell fourteen years in the mountain forest.'
stanzas.hindi: राम ने बिना किसी क्रोध के पिता के वचन का पालन किया: 'पिता के सत्य की रक्षा के लिए मैं चौदह वर्ष वन में निवास करूँगा।'

stanzas.tangkhul: Sitale Lakshman-na Ramli shurkazatta; 'Nali makaleieili shimkhur makalei; kaphungli Ramle pamkasa Iwui kazingramsai.'
stanzas.english: Sita and Lakshmana walked beside him: 'Where Rama is, there is home; to walk the mountain forest with Rama is heaven itself.'
stanzas.hindi: सीता और लक्ष्मण उनके संग चले: 'जहाँ राम हैं वहीं घर है; राम के संग वन में रहना ही स्वर्ग है।'

kandas.title: Aranya Kanda: Panchavatili Pamkasa kala Khara-kashang (The Forest Hermitage & Abduction)
kandas.hindi_title: अरण्य काण्ड: पंचवटी, स्वर्ण मृग एवं सीता हरण
kandas.summary: Dwelling peacefully at Panchavati by the Godavari. Ravana plots vengeance and sends demon Maricha as a dazzling golden deer. While Rama and Lakshmana chase the deer, Ravana abducts Sita. Brave vulture Jatayu battles heroically in the sky.

stanzas.tangkhul: Panchavatili Marichana khara-kashang thada ngasasa; Sita-na khara chi theilaga Ramli 'Ili khuimilu' da hosa.
stanzas.english: At Panchavati, Maricha transformed into a glistening golden deer; seeing it, Sita pleaded with Rama to capture it.
stanzas.hindi: पंचवटी में मारीच ने सुनहले हिरण का रूप धरा; उसे देखकर सीता ने राम से उस हिरण को लाने का आग्रह किया।

stanzas.tangkhul: Lanka-wui Ravana-na Sita-li ngathumta khuisai; vanao Jatayu-na kazei eina ror-la kathi-shoksa Ramli pao mikhavai.
stanzas.english: Ravana deceitfully carried Sita away; the noble bird Jatayu fought valiantly in the clouds until mortally wounded to report to Rama.
stanzas.hindi: रावण ने कपट से सीता का हरण किया; पक्षीराज जटायु ने आकाश में भीषण युद्ध किया और राम को समाचार देने तक प्राण साधे रखे।

kandas.title: Sundara Kanda: Hanuman-na Ngayili Kapai (Hanuman's Leap & Finding Sita in Lanka)
kandas.hindi_title: सुंदर काण्ड: हनुमान जी का समुद्र लांघना एवं लंका दहन
kandas.summary: Hanuman leaps across the roaring ocean to Lanka. He finds mother Sita grieving under the Ashoka tree, delivers Rama's signet ring, reassures her, demonstrates his immense strength, and burns proud Lanka with his flaming tail.

stanzas.tangkhul: Hanuman-na Ramwui ming phaningda ngayi-kharei kapaisai; Ashoka thing-khurli Sitali samphanglaga Ramwui chabi-ring misai.
stanzas.english: Chanting Rama's sacred name, Hanuman leapt across the boundless ocean; beneath the Ashoka tree he found weeping Sita and delivered Rama's signet ring.
stanzas.hindi: राम का नाम स्मरण कर हनुमान ने विशाल समुद्र लांघ लिया; अशोक वाटिका में विरही सीता को खोजकर राम की मुद्रिका भेंट की।

stanzas.tangkhul: Ravana-wui shimkhurli Hanumanna awui meiphu-kuisam eina mei ngapharsai; Lanka-ram saikora meikhu thada ngapharsa.
stanzas.english: In Ravana's palace, Hanuman set his tail ablaze, turning proud Lanka into a blazing torch of smoke and flame.
stanzas.hindi: रावण के महल में हनुमान ने अपनी पूंछ की मशाल से सोने की अभिमानी लंका में आग लगा दी।

kandas.title: Yuddha Kanda: Lanka-wui Rai kala Ram-Rajya (The Great Battle & Reign of Righteousness)
kandas.hindi_title: युद्ध काण्ड: सेतु निर्माण, रावण वध एवं राम-राज्य
kandas.summary: Building the stone bridge across the ocean with the Vanara army. Epic war between the armies of Dharma and Adharma. Rama slays Ravana with the Brahmastra. Sita is reunited; victorious return to Ayodhya for the coronation of Ram-Rajya.

stanzas.tangkhul: Lung-tara eina ngayili shongfa kashapsai; Ramna Brahmastra kazei eina Ravana-li chathatsai; mashunkasana ngamhaira.
stanzas.english: A floating bridge of stone was laid across the ocean; Rama released the supreme Brahmastra arrow, vanquishing Ravana and establishing the eternal victory of truth.
stanzas.hindi: तैरते पत्थरों से समुद्र पर सेतु बांधा गया; राम ने ब्रह्मास्त्र चलाकर रावण का संहार किया और असत्य पर सत्य की विजय स्थापित की।

stanzas.tangkhul: Ayodhyali Ramna Awungatui phungsai; Ram-Rajyali mi saikora ringphada, kathi-kachot makaleida mashunta pamsai.
stanzas.english: Rama was crowned king in joyful Ayodhya; in Ram-Rajya, all citizens lived in peace, righteousness, health, and harmony.
stanzas.hindi: अयोध्या में श्रीराम का राज्याभिषेक हुआ; राम-राज्य में प्रजा सुखी, निरोगी और धर्मपरायण होकर शांति से जीने लगी।

parvas.title: Adi Parva: Pandav Phanga wui Naokaphok (Birth of the Pandavas & Training)
parvas.hindi_title: आदि पर्व: पाँच पाण्डवों का जन्म एवं लक्ष्य वेध
parvas.summary: In Hastinapur, five virtuous Pandava brothers are born: Yudhishthira, Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula, and Sahadeva. Trained in warfare by Master Dronacharya. Arjuna excels all princes by piercing the spinning target eye at Draupadi's Swayamvara.

stanzas.tangkhul: Hastinapurli Pandav phanga leisai: Yudhishthira, Bhima, Arjun, Nakul, Sahadev; athum saikora mashunkasa phungda leisai.
stanzas.english: In Hastinapur lived the five noble Pandava brothers, upholding righteousness and valor.
stanzas.hindi: हस्तिनापुर में पाँच धर्मपरायण पाण्डव भाई जन्मे, जो सत्य, पराक्रम और शील के धनी थे।

stanzas.tangkhul: Draupadi-wui Swayamvarli Arjurna tara-ngathangli khayangda khai-wui amikli kazei eina thut-kakhuisai.
stanzas.english: At Draupadi's Swayamvara, Arjuna gazed into the water reflection and pierced the fish's eye above, winning the princess.
stanzas.hindi: द्रौपदी के स्वयंवर में अर्जुन ने जल में परछाई देखकर मत्स्य की आँख में अचूक बाण मारा।

parvas.title: Sabha & Vana Parva: Shak-kashak kala Kaphungli Kazat (The Dice Game & Forest Exile)
parvas.hindi_title: सभा एवं वन पर्व: द्यूत सभा, चीर हरण एवं १२ वर्ष वनवास
parvas.summary: Duryodhana and Shakuni challenge Yudhishthira to a rigged dice game. Yudhishthira loses realm, wealth, and Draupadi. Krishna miraculously protects Draupadi's dignity with unending fabric. The Pandavas endure twelve years in deep wilderness.

stanzas.tangkhul: Shakunina shak-kashakli ngathumta Yudhishthirali ngamsai; Draupadi-li kachon shat-kaphungli Krishnana kachon-khamatei misai.
stanzas.english: Through deceitful dice Shakuni defeated Yudhishthira; when disrobed in court, Lord Krishna blessed Draupadi with boundless flowing robes.
stanzas.hindi: शकुनि ने कपट से द्यूत में युधिष्ठिर को हराया; भरी सभा में चीरहरण के समय भगवान कृष्ण ने अक्षय वस्त्र देकर द्रौपदी की लाज बचाई।

stanzas.tangkhul: Pandav-bingna kaphung-khurli thara-khani kum pamsai, thing-won kashai chāda, ning-kachang mashun kasasai.
stanzas.english: The Pandavas spent twelve winters in the harsh forest, living on wild roots while deepening their spiritual disciplines.
stanzas.hindi: पाण्डवों ने बारह वर्ष घने जंगलों में कंद-मूल खाकर धर्म और तपस्या के साथ व्यतीत किए।

parvas.title: Udyoga & Bhishma Parva: Kurukshetrawui Rai (Krishna's Peace Mission & War)
parvas.hindi_title: उद्योग एवं भीष्म पर्व: कृष्ण की शांति दूत यात्रा एवं कुरुक्षेत्र युद्ध
parvas.summary: Krishna journeys to Hastinapur pleading for peace, asking merely five villages for the Pandavas. Duryodhana arrogantly rejects. Both armies assemble on Kurukshetra. Grandfather Bhishma leads the Kaurava army for ten days.

stanzas.tangkhul: Krishnana shimlutli vāda 'Khangachee makaleieili ram phanga milu' hosa; Duryodhana-na kazei-amik khatkha maminana.
stanzas.english: Krishna went as peaceful envoy: 'To avoid catastrophe, grant merely five villages.' Duryodhana refused even a needle-point of land.
stanzas.hindi: श्रीकृष्ण शांति दूत बनकर गए: 'विनाश रोकने के लिए केवल पाँच गाँव दे दो।' दुर्योधन ने सुई की नोक बराबर भूमि भी देने से इनकार कर दिया।

stanzas.tangkhul: Kurukshetra ngaleili rai-kharei sasai; Bhishma awunga kazei-chāpui-li tulu; mashunkasana makaphāli ngamsai.
stanzas.english: The supreme battle raged upon Kurukshetra; grandfather Bhishma fell upon a bed of arrows; righteousness overcame darkness.
stanzas.hindi: कुरुक्षेत्र के मैदान में अठारह दिन महायुद्ध चला; पितामह भीष्म बाणों की शय्या पर गिरे और अंततः धर्म की अधर्म पर विजय हुई।

parvas.title: Shanti Parva: Yudhishthira Awunga kala Mashunkasa (Reign of Peace & Duty)
parvas.hindi_title: शांति पर्व: युधिष्ठिर का राज्याभिषेक एवं राजधर्म
parvas.summary: Yudhishthira is crowned in Hastinapur. Dying Bhishma imparts the immortal discourse on righteous governance, compassion for subjects, and universal moral truth.

stanzas.tangkhul: Bhishmana kathi-ranglikha Yudhishthirali wungtui chitheisai; 'Awungana mi saikorali awui naomayar thada mayonlu; mashunkasana awungatuiwui yumshangsai.'
stanzas.english: From his arrow bed Bhishma instructed Yudhishthira: 'A true sovereign must cherish his people as his own children; righteousness is the sole foundation of the throne.'
stanzas.hindi: शरशय्या से भीष्म ने युधिष्ठिर को राजधर्म सिखाया: 'राजा अपनी प्रजा को अपनी संतान समझे; सत्य और धर्म ही राजसिंहासन के स्तम्भ हैं।'

bhagavad_gita.title: Shrimad Bhagavad Gita in Tangkhul Naga: Krishna eina Arjunwui Tui-Ngazek
bhagavad_gita.hindi_title: तंगखुल श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता (श्रीकृष्ण-अर्जुन संवाद: कर्मयोग, भक्तियोग एवं ज्ञानयोग)
bhagavad_gita.author: Vyasa / Traditional Trans-lingual Documentation (CIIL & Bharatavani)

chapters.title: Arjunwui Ning-kashiman (Arjuna's Despondency / अर्जुन विषाद योग)

verses.tangkhul: Arjunna hosa: 'Krishna, iwui kinbingli ror-khavai theilaga iwui phei-apang ngasasa, iwui Gandiva kazei pashok-haowa.'
verses.english: Arjuna cried: 'O Krishna, seeing my own kinsmen gathered for slaughter, my limbs tremble, my mouth parches, and my bow Gandiva slips from my hand.'
verses.hindi: अर्जुन बोले: 'हे कृष्ण! युद्ध में उपस्थित स्वजनों को देखकर मेरे अंग शिथिल हो रहे हैं और गांडीव धनुष हाथ से गिर रहा है।'

chapters.title: Sankhya Yoga: Ning-ringkapha kala Kaza-thei (The Eternal Soul & Wisdom / सांख्य योग)

verses.tangkhul: Mangkhap-hi naokaphok makalei, kathi makalei; kazeina thik-la, meina kakang-la, chi mathi-mana; thing-kachon thada aphur ngacheeya.
verses.english: The soul is never born, nor does it die; weapons cannot pierce it, fire cannot burn it; as one discards old garments for new, the soul casts off worn bodies.
verses.hindi: आत्मा न कभी जन्मती है और न कभी मरती है; न शस्त्र इसे काट सकते हैं, न आग इसे जला सकती है; जैसे मनुष्य पुराने वस्त्र त्यागकर नए पहनता है, वैसे ही आत्मा नया शरीर धारण करती है।

verses.tangkhul: Nawui ot-hi mashunta salu, kha awui kaphawui amik ma-khayang-alu; ot-kasa wui kaza-thei chili ma-nganip-alu.
verses.english: Thy right is to work only, never to its fruits; let not the fruit of action be thy motive, nor let thy attachment be to inaction.
verses.hindi: कर्म पर ही तेरा अधिकार है, फल पर कभी नहीं; इसलिए फल की इच्छा से कर्म मत कर, और न ही कर्म त्यागने का मोह रख।

chapters.title: Karma Yoga: Kasam-mashun wui Tui (The Yoga of Selfless Action / कर्म योग)

verses.tangkhul: Chiwangteina ning-kachang kachi makaleida nawui mashun ot-hi salu; khipakha ot mashunta sa-eili Varivarali phang-ya.
verses.english: Therefore, constantly perform thy obligatory duty without attachment; for by doing work without attachment, man attains the Supreme.
verses.hindi: अतः अनासक्त होकर निरंतर अपने कर्तव्य कर्म का भली-भांति पालन कर; क्योंकि निष्काम कर्म करते हुए मनुष्य परमात्मा को प्राप्त होता है।

chapters.title: Jnana Karma Sannyasa Yoga: Mashunkasa kazip-khavai (Incarnation for Righteousness / ज्ञान संन्यास योग)

verses.tangkhul: Khitharan mashunkasa makaleilaga makaphāna phung-eili, Arjun, Ina okathuili naoshok-ra; mashunkasabingli mayon-khavai kala makaphābingli chathat-khavai.
verses.english: Whenever there is a decline of righteousness and an uprising of unrighteousness, then I manifest Myself, O Arjuna, to protect the good and destroy evil.
verses.hindi: यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत। जब-जब धर्म की हानि और अधर्म की वृद्धि होती है, तब-तब मैं सज्जनों की रक्षा और दुष्टों के विनाश के लिए प्रकट होता हूँ।

chapters.title: Raja Vidya Yoga: Varivara wui Tui (The Sovereign Secret / राजविद्या योग)

verses.tangkhul: Khipakha Ina leishida thing-kup akha, won akha, thei akha, tara akha-tara mili-kha, I ningphada khuira.
verses.english: Whoever offers Me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or even water, that gift offered with a pure heart, I accept with gladness.
verses.hindi: पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं - जो भक्त मुझे प्रेम से एक पत्ता, फूल, फल या केवल जल भी अर्पित करता है, उस शुद्ध हृदय के उपहार को मैं सहर्ष स्वीकार करता हूँ।

chapters.title: Vishvarupa Darshana Yoga: Zingkum-saikora Amai Kathei (The Cosmic Vision / विश्वरूप दर्शन योग)

verses.tangkhul: Kazingli zimik thing-akha akha-eina ngaphar-thada, Ishawui amai kashak-chi chithada ngapharsai; Arjun-na khayangda khurak-hai-sai.
verses.english: If the radiance of a thousand suns were to burst at once into the sky, that would be like the splendor of the Mighty One; seeing it, Arjuna bowed in awe.
verses.hindi: यदि आकाश में सहस्र सूर्यों का तेज एक साथ उदय हो, तो वह परम पुरुष के उस विश्वरूप के प्रकाश के सदृश हो सकता है।

chapters.title: Moksha Sannyasa Yoga: Mashunli Ngakhum (Liberation through Surrender / मोक्ष संन्यास योग)

verses.tangkhul: Saikora horkahaida I-li ngakhum-lu; Ina nali kashiman saikora wui eina huikhuira; ma-ngachee-alu!
verses.english: Abandon all varieties of dharmas and just surrender unto Me alone; I shall deliver thee from all sins; do not grieve!
verses.hindi: सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज। सब धर्मों का आश्रय छोड़कर केवल मेरी शरण में आ जाओ; मैं तुम्हें समस्त पापों व संतापों से मुक्त कर दूँगा, शोक मत करो!

prayers_and_invocations.title: Tangkhul Traditional Prayers & Invocations (Hai-kapha kala Seikha-kapha)
prayers_and_invocations.title_translation: Comprehensive Compendium of Tangkhul Invocations, Blessing Prayers, and Sacred Chants
prayers_and_invocations.creator: Tangkhul Community Elders & Traditional Invocators
prayers_and_invocations.notes: Comprehensive documentation of traditional Tangkhul invocations (Hai-kapha) and blessing chants (Seikha-kapha) addressed to the Supreme Creator (Varivara), mountain spirits, hearth dedication, agricultural blessings, and ancestral spirits.

prayer_sections.section_title: Varivara-li Hai-kapha: Invocations to the Supreme Creator
prayer_sections.ritual_context: Solemn dawn invocations addressed to the Creator of heaven and earth during village convocations.

prayers.prayer_name: Kazing kala Ngalei Kasa Akhavara (Sovereign of Heaven and Earth)
prayers.tangkhul: Varivara, kazing kala ngalei kasa akhavara! Iram Hunphun kala Tangkhul ngaleili kapha eina leishat kachung khami. Macham-matai, kazingwui ringkapha kala ngaleiwui kachon shim kachivali shung-ngasak-lu.
prayers.english: O Varivara, Sovereign Creator of heaven and earth! Bestow goodness and overflowing love upon Hunphun and all Tangkhul lands. Let the peace of heaven and the fruitfulness of the earth fill every home.
prayers.hindi: हे वरिवरा, स्वर्ग और पृथ्वी के सृष्टिकर्ता परमेश्वर! हमारे हुंफुन गांव और संपूर्ण तंगखुल भूमि पर अपनी भलाई और असीम अनुग्रह बरसाएं। हर घर को स्वर्गीय शांति और पृथ्वी की उर्वरता से परिपूर्ण करें।

prayers.prayer_name: Ringkaphawui Ning-Ngazek (Petition for Life, Health, and Unity)
prayers.tangkhul: Iramwui mayar-shanao kachivali kapha kakhanganuina ninglum-hai-lu; kacham-kahao maningda, maram-matai eina ngachee kachiva machik-hai-lu.
prayers.english: Endow all the sons and daughters of our land with righteous discernment and upright character; banish famine and poverty, and protect us from every calamity.
prayers.hindi: हमारी भूमि के सभी पुत्र-पुत्रियों को धार्मिक विवेक और सदाचार से सुशोभित करें; अकाल व दरिद्रता को दूर रखें और हर विपत्ति से हमारी रक्षा करें।

prayer_sections.section_title: Luira Shimlut-wui Seikha: Agrarian Sowing & Harvest Invocations
prayer_sections.ritual_context: Chanted at dawn by the Awunga (chief) turning the first sod of earth during Luira Phanit.

prayers.prayer_name: Shimlut Kaphung Invocatory Chant (First Seed Blessing)
prayers.tangkhul: Tara-kong kala kaphung ngalemwui makhangai ngachaili, kachang kathara eina phung-kasa oira. Kachim-kasa mayar-shanao mashung-ngasak-lu; changva kachon kachivali mathala kaza samphang-ngasak-lu.
prayers.english: By the quiet mountain streams and along terraced slopes, let the newly sown seeds take deep root in fertile earth. Bless the labor of men and women; may every sheaf harvested bring joyful sustenance.
prayers.hindi: पर्वतीय जलधाराओं और ढलानों पर बोए गए नए बीजों को उपजाऊ धरती में गहराई से फलने-फूलने का आशीर्वाद दें। सभी पुरुषों और महिलाओं के श्रम को सफल करें; हर बाली प्रचुर अन्न और सुख प्रदान करे।

prayers.tangkhul: Chumkhur hili kashung tara-chang, kacham kashiman malailaka; shanao mibingwui pāng eina phung-kasa za-machit mashung-ngasak-lu.
prayers.english: May the grain stored in this sacred granary endure through every season, banishing all want; through the blessed hands of women custodians, let our sustenance never fail.
prayers.hindi: इस पवित्र अन्न भंडार में संचित अनाज हर ऋतु में बना रहे और हर अभाव को दूर करे; अन्न की संरक्षिका मातृशक्ति के हाथों से हमारी संपन्नता कभी कम न हो।

prayer_sections.section_title: Shimsa kala Meiphung Invocations: Hearth & Domestic Protection
prayer_sections.ritual_context: Chanted during the dedication of a newly built house when kindling the sacred hearth fire.

prayers.tangkhul: Meiphung kathara hili mei-ngatai eina ngachee kachiva machik-hai-lu. Shimwui naonao kala marva ningcha-ngachan eina khararchan wui tui kathara thotkakhui mashung-ngasak-lu.
prayers.english: Around this consecrated hearth, kindle the sacred fire to dispel darkness, sickness, and strife. May the children and elders of this household dwell in unity and pass down ancestral virtues across generations.
prayers.hindi: इस पवित्र चूल्हे पर प्रज्वलित अग्नि समस्त अंधकार, व्याधि और कलह को दूर करे। इस घर के बच्चे और वृद्धजन एकता में रहें और पूर्वजों के संस्कारों को पीढ़ी-दर-पीढ़ी आगे बढ़ाएं।

prayer_sections.section_title: Khayang Shongfa Hai-kapha: Mountain Wilderness & Wayfarer Blessing
prayer_sections.ritual_context: Uttered before undertaking mountain expeditions, hunting journeys, or cross-valley trade.

prayers.prayer_name: Shongfa Makhangai Prayer (Safe Passage Across Mountain Ridges)
prayers.tangkhul: Kaphung kachang, kongrei kala thang-khala shongfali yaokhayei eina kacham-kahao maning-ngasak-lu. Awungana iram-iramli macham kashap samphang-ngasak-lu.
prayers.english: Across high mountain ridges, turbulent torrents, and wilderness trails, grant sure footing and keep all danger afar. May the traveler return home bearing peace and honor.
prayers.hindi: ऊंचे पर्वतों, उफनती नदियों और बीहड़ वन्य मार्गों पर हमारे कदमों को स्थिरता दें और सभी विपत्तियों से रक्षा करें। यात्री कुशलतापूर्वक शांति और सम्मान के साथ घर लौटें।

prayer_sections.section_title: Thisham Kasa Akhava Hai-kapha: Ancestral Memorial Chants
prayer_sections.ritual_context: Chanted by village elders lighting pine-splint torches during Thisham Phanit (Feast of Departing Souls).

prayers.prayer_name: Kasa Akhava Chanted Requiem (Farewell to Departed Ancestors)
prayers.tangkhul: Kasa Akhava kaphungli va-kahai araza, meira kaphit hieina shongfa theingasak-lu. Ningkacham eina mangachon-hai-lu; ringphawui ramli mashungda leisang-lu.
prayers.english: O revered departed ancestors journeying toward Kasa Akhava (the ancestral spirit realm), let these flaming pine torches illuminate your path. Rest in tranquil grace; enter the eternal land of blessed peace.
prayers.hindi: हे पूर्वजों की आत्माओं, कासा अखावा (परम लोक) की यात्रा पर इन पाइन की मशालों के उजाले में अपना मार्ग प्रशस्त करें। दिव्य शांति में विश्राम करें और शाश्वत सुख के धाम में प्रवेश करें।

rituals_and_ceremonies.title: Tangkhul Sacred Rituals, Ceremonies & Taboos (Phanit, Kakhangaso kala Khamasit)
rituals_and_ceremonies.title_translation: Master Archive of Tangkhul Lifecycle Ceremonies, Agrarian Rites, and Sacred Taboo Observances
rituals_and_ceremonies.creator: Tangkhul Hereditary Custodians & Village Elders
rituals_and_ceremonies.notes: Comprehensive archival codification of Tangkhul ceremonial life: agrarian seasonal rites (Luira, Chumpha, Mangkhap, Dharreo), human lifecycle rituals (birth, naming, youth dormitory induction, marriage, house dedication, death), prestige feast cycles (Maran Kasa), chiefly enthronement, and sacred taboo (Khamasit / Genna) observances.

rites.name: Luira Shimlut-kaphung (First Sowing Rite)
rites.description: At dawn on the first day of Luira Phanit, the chief turns the ceremonial first clod of earth and sows seeds before any villager may begin cultivation, accompanied by libations and wrestling (Kaphung).
rites.significance: Sanctifies communal agriculture and establishes cosmological harmony between the soil and the village lineage.

rites.name: Chumkhur Kakhon (Granary Consecration Rite)
rites.description: Ceremonial unlocking and fumigation of the granary (Chum); ritual transfer of keys and first invocation of blessing over newly harvested rice.
rites.significance: Honors women as custodians of grain, life, and domestic prosperity in Tangkhul custom.

rites.name: Mangkhap Kaphung (Transplantation Rest Rite)
rites.description: Communal purification of spade, hoe, and sickle; ceremonial consumption of fermented rice brew (Khor); seven-day period of agricultural stillness.
rites.significance: Allows fields and bodies to recuperate; prevents early pestilence through ritual rest.

rites.name: Dharreo Invocations (Pre-Harvest Shielding Rite)
rites.description: Placement of ceremonial bamboo charms around terraced perimeters to ward off unseasonable hail, violent gales, and rodent swarms.
rites.significance: Guarantees that the golden harvest reaches the granaries unmolested by natural calamities.

rites.name: Naothara Kaphok & Samkhui (Birth, Naming & Ear-Piercing)
rites.description: Newborn infant purificatory bath; severance of umbilical cord with sterile bamboo blade; divination of ancestral clan name (Shang wui Ming); ceremonial ear-piercing.
rites.significance: Integrates the newborn into the patrilineal clan and ancestral cosmological lineage.

rites.name: Longshim Induction Ceremony
rites.description: Formal entrance into Mayarshim (boys dormitory) or Ngashim (girls dormitory); presentation of first handwoven Haora or Kashan attire; instruction in martial defense, weaving, and oral songs.
rites.significance: Civic graduation from domestic dependence to communal responsibility and village defense.

rites.name: Manom & Shimlut (Customary Marriage Rites)
rites.description: Formal betrothal negotiation between exogamous clans; presentation of bridal attire (Chonkhom, Seichan) and bronze gongs (Sanam); nuptial banquet and elder blessings.
rites.significance: Binds two distinct clans in perpetual mutual covenant and socio-economic alliance.

rites.name: Shimsa (House Dedication & Hearth Consecration)
rites.timing: Upon completion of a new timber dwelling
rites.description: Ritual kindling of the new hearth fire using traditional flint stones (Meitai); libation of rice beer at threshold; installation of protective ancestral charms.
rites.significance: Transforms physical architecture into a living sanctum protected by ancestral spirits.

rites.name: Thisham Phanit (The Great Memorial Feast of the Dead)
rites.presiding: Clan Lineage Heads & Departed Souls Custodians
rites.description: Ten-day solemn festival commemorating all souls deceased during the year; lighting of resinous pine torches (Meira Kaphit) to guide souls to Kasa Akhava; farewell banquet.
rites.significance: Ensures that departed spirits transition peacefully to the ancestral spirit realm without lingering in distress.

rites.name: Maran Kasa (The Multi-Stage Feast of Merit)
rites.presiding: Benefactor Couple, Awunga & Entire Village Council
rites.description: Five-tier progressive feast cycle hosting the entire village; sacrificial feast of mithun and cattle; confers the lifelong privilege of erecting the horned Tarang post and Lengcheng roof structure.

clans_and_social_structure.notes: Foundational sociological and anthropological study of Tangkhul Naga social structure. Clarifies the complete absence of a caste system, examining instead the democratic patrilineal clan (Shang / Shangnao) structure, strict clan exogamy, village governance (Awunga and Hangva council), and youth dormitory institutions (Longshim).

sociological_framework.caste_clarification: The Tangkhul Naga people do NOT have a caste (varna or jati) system. Tangkhul society is fundamentally egalitarian, democratic, and non-hierarchical with respect to hereditary servitude. Social organization is instead governed by ancient patrilineal clans (Shang or Shangnao), clan exogamy, and village council democracy.
principles_of_kinship: Patrilineal Descent: Clan membership and ancestral land inheritance pass through the male lineage.

Strict Clan Exogamy (Shang wui Shimlut): Marriage between individuals of the same clan (Shang) is strictly forbidden. A breach of this law is termed 'Masi-kongra' (spiritual pollution requiring heavy customary purification and possible exile).
Complementary Clan Alliances: Matrimonial unions create binding socio-economic covenants between complementary clans across and within villages.

Egalitarian Wealth Redistribution: Wealthy villagers do not oppress poorer members; through the 'Maran Kasa' (Feast of Merit), wealth is communally consumed and redistributed, earning social honor rather than coercive dominion.
